MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE LOMITA CITY COUNCIL
January 6, 2014

1.  OPENING CEREMONIES

a.  Call Meeting to Order

A regular meeting of the Lomita City Council was called to order at 7:00 p.m., on
Monday, January 6, 2014, in the Council Chambers, at Lomita City Hall, 24300
Narbonne Avenue.

b.  Flag Salute

Councilmember Savidan led the salute to the flag.

c.  Invocation

Councilmember Waronek gave the invocation.

d.  Roll Call

Those responding to roll call by Assistant City Clerk Shumway were
COUNCILMEMBERS: Gazeley, Traina, Waronek, Sanchez, and Mayor Savidan. Also
present were City Manager Rock, Assistant City Manager Sugano, City Attorney Hogin,
Community Services Director McPherron, Parks and Recreation Director Harding,
Public Works Director Damasse, Administrative Services Director Chavez, and Assistant
City Clerk Shumway.

2.  PRESENTATIONS

Mayor Savidan and Councilmembers recognized Chris Dunn for winning first place at
the Giant Pumpkin Weigh-Off & Contest at the 2013 Pumpkinmania at Tanaka Farms.

City Manager Rock recognized Mayor Savidan for his twenty five years of service to the
City of Lomita. Mayor Savidan stated that he would also donate the cost of the service
award (watch) he received to the City’s Parks and Recreation Program.

3.  APPROVAL OF AGENDA

Councilmember Gazeley moved to approve the agenda.  Councilmember Sanchez
seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.

  Page 1
 4. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

Joe McGrath, Lomita resident, asked that City Council consider establishing regulations
for the sale and distribution of electronic cigarettes in the City. Mr. McGrath also spoke
about the Los Angeles Regional Imagery Acquisition Consortium, and recommended
that the City participate in the program. And, in regards to Consent Agenda Item #7.N,
Mr. McGrath stated that the settlement agreement amount seemed insufficient in order
to cover all associated deficiencies and legal costs.

George Kivett, Lomita resident, thanked Christine Ortiz, Senior Neighborhood
Preservation Officer for being efficient in the removal of graffiti in the City. Mr. Kivett
also spoke on the issue of abandoned shopping carts in the City, as well as the non-
operational crosswalk on Narbonne Avenue.

Scott Mann, Lomita resident, expressed his appreciation to City Council and City staff
for the street repairs completed adjacent to his residence, and he submitted a letter of
appreciation for the record.

5. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS AND MEETING ATTENDANCE REPORTS FROM THE
  CITY COUNCIL

Councilmember Traina requested a future agenda item to discuss the possibility of
establishing a written purchasing policy regarding the selection of Lomita businesses
over out-of-town businesses, as long as local businesses provide competitive pricing.
Councilmember Sanchez supported the motion. Councilmember Gazeley stated that he
would not support the motion, as sometimes there is a problem with finding the right and
best priced product in Lomita; furthermore, Councilmember Gazeley stated that staff
already has a rule to shop in Lomita whenever possible. Mayor Savidan agreed with
Councilmember Gazeley. City Manager Rock stated that City staff tries to make
purchases in Lomita first, but that it is difficult at times to find the best prices.
Councilmember Traina reiterated that staff needs to be encouraged to shop in Lomita
first, as long as it is competitive to do so. The request for a future agenda item failed for
the lack of three votes.

Councilmember Traina requested two additional future agenda items to discuss: the
establishment of regulations regarding the sale and distribution of electronic cigarettes
in Lomita, and the City’s potential participation in the Los Angeles Regional Imagery
Acquisition Consortium. Councilmember Sanchez agreed to place the request for
potential participation in the Los Angeles Regional Imagery Acquisition Consortium on a
future agenda. Councilmembers Gazeley, Waronek, and Mayor Savidan stated that in
order for them to place the requests on a future agenda, they would need to conduct a
little more research regarding the issues. Both requests for future agenda items failed

  Page 2
 for the lack of three votes.

Councilmember Waronek thanked the staff of the Parks and Recreation Department for
a very well organized Tree Lightening Ceremony. Councilmember Waronek also
reported that he attended the 47th Annual Contract Cities Legislative Orientation Tour.

Councilmember Sanchez reported that he attended a meeting of the League of
California Cities on January 2, 2014, at which the future of Los Angeles transit was the
main topic of discussion.

Councilmember Gazeley invited all Councilmembers and the City Manager to attend the
upcoming South Bay Cities Council of Governments (SBCCOG) Strategic Planning
Workshop on January 9, 2014. Councilmember Gazeley also reported that he attended
a meeting of the Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) on January 2,
2014.

6. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

City Manager Rock provided an update regarding the crosswalk on Narbonne Avenue,
and stated that staff has taken steps to properly mark the crosswalk as non-operational.
According to City Manager Rock, recommendations and cost estimates for the
crosswalk modernization/repair will be presented to the City Council at a future meeting.

City Manager Rock reported that he attended a meeting on December 16, 2013,
regarding power outages and power reliability in the South Bay, and according to City
Manager Rock, it was agreed that a report will be prepared for each city in the South
Bay regarding such issue, and posted on the internet during the first quarter of 2014.

7. CONSENT AGENDA

Councilmember Gazeley moved to approve the Consent Agenda. Councilmember
Waronek seconded the motion. Councilmember Traina requested to pull Items 7.C, 7.E,
7.L, and 7.N for discussion. Councilmember Sanchez requested to pull Item 7.M for
discussion. The motion to approve the remainder of the items on the Consent Agenda
was approved unanimously.

Item 7.C - In regards to Voucher #511877, Councilmember Traina asked for clarification
about why services from WaterWorks had been requested given that the City has the
full-time Water Treatment Operator. Responding to Councilmember Traina, Public
Works Director Damasse stated that the City utilizes WaterWorks as a back-up to the
Water Treatment Operator, and to provide on-site refresher training for City staff. In
response to Councilmember Traina’s question regarding levels of ammonia as

  Page 3
 indicated in WaterWorks report, Public Works Director Damasse responded that the City
is required to maintain certain ammonia ratio as optimum, and WaterWorks were
modifying the system in order to establish that optimum ratio for ammonia levels.
Councilmember Traina moved to approve Item 7.C.  Councilmember Sanchez
seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.

In regards to Voucher #511866, Councilmember Sanchez stated that the amount being
paid to Sharp Electronics Corporation seemed a little high. Assistant City Manager
Sugano responded to Councilmember Sanchez’s inquiry by stating that the approved
lease agreement is for 39 months, which in turn resulted in a low lease cost, and
Assistant City Clerk Shumway added that the invoice amount is for two months, which
also includes the cost of printed copies.

Item 7.E – In response to Councilmember Traina’s question regarding the planned
upgrades to the Community Room in the Tom Rico Center, Assistant City Manager
Sugano responded that the cost for those upgrades will be covered by grant monies
received from Supervisor Knabe’s Office, in the amount $150,000. Councilmember
Traina moved to approve Item 7.E. Councilmember Sanchez seconded the motion,
which carried unanimously.

Item 7.L – Councilmember Traina stated that the cassette tapes of City Council
meetings should be treated as historical documents, and in turn recommended that they
be given to the to the Historical Society, instead of being destroyed. Discussion
followed on whether Council would like to convert the cassettes to DVDs, or to keep
them as historical records. Councilmember Waronek stated that the minutes of City
Council meetings are the permanent and official records of such meetings, even if the
cassettes are destroyed. Councilmember Traina again reiterated his opposition to
destroying the cassettes, and recommended keeping them. City Attorney Hogin stated
that Council could remove the first item (cassette tapes) from Exhibit A, and direct staff
to see if the Historical Society would be interested in taking the cassettes, and if the
Historical Society is not interested, then staff could come up with some other
possibilities. Councilmember Traina moved to approve Item 7.L, with the option and
wording provided by City Attorney Hogin. Councilmember Gazeley seconded the
motion, which carried unanimously.

Item 7.M – Councilmember Sanchez moved to recodify self-storage facilities in the
City’s Municipal Code, but also requested a future agenda item to discuss the allowable
uses of self-storage facilities on Lomita Boulevard and Narbonne Avenue. Furthermore,
Councilmember Sanchez also suggested possibly placing a moratorium on any such
new development until a thorough review is conducted. City Attorney Hogin clarified
that the motion was to approve the recodification of self-storage facilities at this
meeting, but also to direct staff to bring back an ordinance that would prohibit any new

  Page 4
 applications for self-storage facilities, as well as to direct staff to initiate a text
amendment to consider prohibiting any new self-storage facilities in the City.
Councilmember Gazeley seconded the motion.

George Kivett, Lomita resident, spoke in opposition of self-storage facilities in
Commercial-General Zones within the City, and recommended other sites for the
potential development of self-storage facilities.

The motion carried unanimously.

Item 7.N - In response to Councilmember Traina’s question regarding the estimated
amount for repair work at the Cypress Water Production Facility (CWPF), Public Works
Director Damasse responded that the initial estimated amount was $300,000, but the
amount will be finalized once the plans go to bid. Councilmember Traina stated that he
believes that the settlement amount is inadequate, as it does not cover all the
associated repair and legal costs, and that the City should not have to incur any related
costs.

Councilmember Gazeley moved to approve and accept this proposal. Councilmember
Sanchez seconded the motion.

ROLL CALL:
AYES: Councilmembers Gazeley, Sanchez, Waronek, and Mayor Savidan
NOES: Councilmember Traina

  a. Motion to Waive Further Reading

  b. Recommendation to approve the minutes for the Regular City Council meeting and
  the Special City Council meeting held on December 2, 2013. RECOMMEND
  APPROVAL.

  c. Approval of Demands. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  d. Monthly Report for the Administrative Services Department. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  e. Monthly Report for the Community Development Department.  RECEIVE AND
  FILE.

  f. Monthly Report for the Parks and Recreation Department. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  g. Monthly Report for the Public Works Department. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  i. Monthly Report from the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department. RECEIVE

  j. November 2013 Treasurer’s Report. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  k. Second reading and adoption of an Ordinance amending Section 11-1.66.08(D) of

  parking garages from nine (9) feet to 8’2”. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  l. Approval of a Resolution authorizing the destruction of certain City records as
  provided by Section 34090 of the Government Code of the State of California.
  RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  m. Administrative clarification to direct staff to notify the City’s codifier, MuniCode, to

  as a permitted use in the C-G (Commercial, General) zone. RECOMMEND

  n. Approval of a Settlement Agreement and Release with Tetra Tech, Inc. relative to
  the Cypress Water Production Facility (CWPF) in which Tetra Tech will provide
  preliminary review, design services, project management, and $20,000 toward
  certain repairs, retrofits and upgrades of the facility. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  PUBLIC HEARING:

8.  ADOPTION OF AN URGENCY ORDINANCE AND FIRST READING OF AN
  ORDINANCE FOR CODE AMENDMENT NO. 2014-01 REGARDING ADOPTION
  BY REFERENCE OF VARIOUS 2013 LOS ANGELES COUNTY CODES
  RELATED TO STATE BUILDING CODES

  Assistant City Manager Sugano stated that the City contracts with the City of Los
  Angeles for building and safety services, including plan checks for buildings, as well
  as electrical and mechanical-related permits. According to Assistant City Manager
  Sugano, the City has adopted earlier versions of related codes by reference, and in
  turn he recommended the approval of an urgency ordinance adopting, by reference,
  the various 2014 Los Angeles County Construction Codes, including all
  amendments, and to direct staff to schedule the second reading and adoption of the
  proposed ordinance at the next City Council meeting scheduled for January 21,
  2014.

  Discussion followed regarding storm drains, storm water prevention measures, and
  the difference between state and local requirements. Kit Bagnell, a Los Angeles

  Page 6
   County Building Official, provided an explanation regarding the difference between
  storm drains and storm water requirements from a code perspective, as well as
  drainage practices during and after construction.

  Mayor Savidan opened the Public Hearing.  There was no public participation.
  Mayor Savidan closed the Public Hearing.

  Councilmember Gazeley moved to approve the adoption of the urgency ordinance
  and first reading. City Attorney Hogin read the title of the ordinance for the record.
  Councilmember Sanchez seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.

  SCHEDULED ITEMS:

9.  POSSIBLE APPOINTMENT  OF  COMMISSIONERS  TO  THE  PARKS  &
  RECREATION COMMISSION

  Councilmember Traina nominated Bryan Mathews for Parks and Recreation
  Commissioner. Councilmembers Waronek, Savidan, and Sanchez nominated Bob
  Eubanks for Parks and Recreation Commissioner. Bob Eubanks was appointed to
  the Parks and Recreation Commission.

  Councilmembers Gazeley, Sanchez, and Mayor Savidan nominated Peter
  Montgomery, Jr. for Parks and Recreation Commissioner. Peter Montgomery, Jr.
  was re-appointed to the Parks and Recreation Commission.

  Councilmembers Waronek and Traina nominated Bryan Mathews for Parks and
  Recreation Commissioner. Councilmember Gazeley nominated Tommy Bonham for
  Parks and Recreation Commissioner. Councilmember Sanchez nominated Donald
  Thomas for Parks and Recreation Commissioner. Mayor Savidan nominated Bryan
  Mathews for Parks and Recreation Commissioner. Bryan Mathews was appointed
  to the Parks and Recreation Commission.
  th
10. DISCUSSION AND POSSIBLE ACTION ESTABLISHING A 50  ANNIVERSARY
  SUBCOMMITTEE

  Councilmembers Waronek and Gazeley expressed their interest in serving on the
  50th Anniversary Subcommittee, which will plan, organize, and raise money to cover
  the expenses for the celebration. City Council decided that the subcommittee will
  work with the staff of the Parks and Recreation Department, and bring
  recommendations, including any associated expenses, to Council for approval.

11. DISCUSSION  AND CONSIDERATION REGARDING THE POSSIBLE
  RECONVENING OF THE GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE (GPAC)

  Assistant City Manager Sugano stated that General Plan Advisory Committee

  Page 7
   (GPAC) was originally created in 2005, consisted of 17 members, held several
  meetings, adopted a Recommendations Report, and looked at specific issues,
  including a mixed-use ordinance and a thrift store ordinance. According to Assistant
  City Manager Sugano, a comprehensive update of the General Plan would cost
  hundreds of thousands of dollars, with the amount varying based on the scope of
  the proposed update.

  In response to Councilmember Traina’s question regarding how often cities update
  their General Plan, Assistant City Manager Sugano stated that updates are usually
  conducted every 15 or 20 years.  Councilmember Sanchez stated that in
  accordance with the staff report and the GPAC Recommendations Report, City
  Council is supposed to review the recommendations of the GPAC every five years,
  and in turn Councilmember Sanchez recommended: reconvening the GPAC in
  order to review the GPAC Recommendations Report; reduce the number of GPAC
  members to six; have Community Development Staff facilitate GPAC meetings, and
  for the GPAC to provide a report back to City Council. Councilmember Traina
  seconded the motion. Councilmember Gazeley recommended that some Planning
  Commissioners be included on the GPAC. Discussion followed on how many
  Planning Commissioners should be included on the GPAC.

  George Kivett, Lomita resident, spoke in support of the motion and added that it will
  be timely to review of the General Plan at this point.

  City Attorney Hogin restated Councilmember Sanchez’s motion, and additions made
  by Council: to direct staff to create a General Plan Advisory Committee (GPAC)
  consisting of two Planning Commissioners and four former GPAC members; to
  direct the City Manager to recruit and appoint members of the GPAC, who in turn
  will review the GPAC Recommendations Report; for the new GPAC meetings to be
  facilitated by City staff; and GPAC and City staff to report back to City Council on
  how well the recommendations were implemented.  Councilmember Traina
  seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.

12. DISCUSSION AND POSSIBLE DIRECTION CHANGING THE TIME AND DAY OF
  REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETINGS

  Assistant City Manager Sugano stated that on December 2, 2013, City Council
  requested that this item be placed on a future agenda for discussion. Discussion
  followed on whether changing the day of the Council meeting from Monday to
  Tuesday or Wednesday would be feasible and accommodate all Councilmembers’
  schedules. Council decided not to change the day of City Council meetings due to
  schedule conflicts of some Councilmembers. Councilmember Traina stated that
  changing the time of the meeting, from 7:00 p.m. to 6:30 p.m., would make it difficult

  Page 8
   for him to make the Council meetings on time, especially for Special City Council
  meetings, which typically take place before Regular City Council meetings.
  Councilmember Traina asked Council to take his work schedule into consideration
  and try to accommodate his request.

  Joe McGrath, Cindy Segawa, and George Kivett, Lomita residents, spoke in
  opposition of changing the time of City Council meetings.

  Councilmember Gazeley moved to approve changing the start time of Regular City
  Council meetings from 7:00 p.m. to 6:30 p.m. Councilmember Waronek seconded
  the motion.

  ROLL CALL:
  AYES: Councilmembers Sanchez, Waronek, Gazeley, and Mayor Savidan
  NOES: Councilmember Traina

13. CITY COUNCIL POLICY FOR PLACEMENT OF ITEMS ON FUTURE AGENDAS

  City Manager Rock stated that the current practice for placing items on a future
  agenda requires the votes of three Councilmembers. According to City Manager
  Rock, most other City Councils follow the same practice, and those that do not end
  up with lengthy meetings. City Manager Rock recommended that the current
  practice being used by Council for placing items on a future agenda remain in place.

  Joe McGrath and George Kivett, Lomita residents, spoke in opposition of the
  current practice requiring the consent of three Councilmembers in order to place an
  item on a future agenda.

  Councilmember Traina stated that the ability of Councilmembers to place something
  on a future agenda is very important, as sometimes issues need to be acted upon
  quickly; Councilmember Traina went on to provide some examples.

  Councilmember Gazeley stated that the current practice is a very democratic
  process, thereby requiring the majority to agree upon future agenda items.

  Councilmember Gazeley moved to keep the current practice of placing items on a
  future agenda in place.  Councilmember Waronek seconded the motion.
  Councilmember Sanchez stated that in 2012, he suggested allowing each
  Councilmember to have one agenda item per Council meeting. Councilmember
  Traina stated that eliminating the three vote requirement would also simplify the
  Planning Commission appeal process.

  Page 9
   ROLL CALL:
  AYES: Councilmembers Gazeley, Waronek, and Mayor Savidan
  NOES: Councilmembers Traina and Sanchez

Meeting adjourned at 9:02 p.m.

Respectfully Submitted,

__________________________________
Lena Shumway, Assistant City Clerk, CMC
